description: Windows CI coverage classification (issue 776). Every Windows-named, Windows-platform-comparing, or helper-delegated top-level test file is classified: triage a = needs a real Windows runner, b = fully covered on Linux (pure or mocked Windows layer), c = POSIX-only (Windows branches skip by design). invocations record the expected effective Windows commands (job, full-file or exact name filters, required opt-in environment, required earlier step ids); nativeCases bind required native cases to exact declared titles. Enforced by tests/ci-test-platform-manifest.test.ts.

On Windows the drive-path cases (L115, L132, L155, L170) run with no opt-in (SKIP is false whenever win32, L12). The UNC alias cases (L184) are conditional: they skip when the exact owned localhost alias is unavailable (L192-198), and fail instead only under PI_REVIEW_GATE_REQUIRE_WINDOWS_SESSION_HOST=1, which the current alpha step does not set. So today's CI proves the drive paths for certain and the UNC paths only when the alias resolves. No workflow change in this phase; the CI phase may decide whether to set the opt-in.
